title: A solver who expresses a system simply has found the lever, because compression only comes from understanding the structure
body:
- A solver who expresses a solution simply has found the lever in the system, because that compression only comes from grasping the underlying structure.
- Simple expressions are not simplistic — they carry the compressed complexity of the system, with surface detail left behind once the decisive relationships are known.
- Unnecessary complexity in a solution signals the solver may still be carrying unresolved distinctions, exceptions, or mechanisms that block compression, so the simplicity of the expression is itself the proof the work was done.
- Case: E=mc² — the formulation is short because Einstein understood the system, not because the world is itself simple.
conversion: A simple expression becomes evidence the solver grasped the structure, because compression to the decisive relationships is only possible once the lever is known.
